 (SHRI ATUL CHOUDHARI - ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO.1)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed seeking quashment of the private complaint under Section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act filed against the petitioner being registered as Complaint Case No.119/2018 pending before learned Judicial Magistrate First Class Satna (M.P.).
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that the respondent filed a complaint against the petitioner under Dipti Agnihotri vs Smt. Ruchi Agrawal on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130754823/
1 Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred as the 'Act of 1881').

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 is a dealer of the petroleum products of Bharat Petroleum Corporation and runs her business from Lakhampur N.H. - 7, Rewa, District Satna.
Respondent No.2 is the husband of respondent No.1 and helps respondent No.1 in her business.
Applicant is the wife of Shri Santosh Agnihotri who used to purchase Diesel on credit from the respondents.

An amount of Rs.1,95,048/-
was due for which a cheque from the joint account of the applicant amounting to Rs.1,20,000/- of Induslnd Bank Ltd. bearing cheque No.518676 dated 30.11.2017 was issued.
The cheque was dishonored on presentation to the Union Bank of India, Satna for the reason insufficient funds.
3. On notice being issued the assurance was given by the respondents that if the cheque is again put in the Bank the same will be honored.
But, the same was again dishonored for the reason insufficient funds.
Thereafter, a complaint has been filed.

The application seeking exemption from the proceedings under Section 138 of the Act of 1881 has been filed on the ground that she is neither the signatory of the cheque in question nor any obligation to pay the cheque amount.
She has been made accused in the complaint merely because the cheque was issued from the joint account.
The learned trial court has rejected the application on 06.11.2019.
Therefore, this petition has been filed.
4. It is argued that the cheque in question has been signed by her husband Santosh Agnihotri.
Although the same has been given from the joint account of applicant as well as her husband, but the fact remains that she has no signed the cheque in question.
Therefore, she cannot be held liable for making the payments.
The cheque does not belong to any firm or any company.
It is a cheque with joint account holdings.
Therefore, the signatory of the cheque is liable to repay the amount.
She is unnecessarily dragged into the proceedings of Section 138 of the Act of 1881.

5. He has placed reliance upon the judgment dated 30.11.2023 passed in the case of Shalu Arora v.
Tanu Bathla : CRM. No.21798/2022 by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh and in the case of Aparna A. Shah v. M/s Sheth Developers Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. :1 Criminal Appeal No.813/2023 decided on 01.07.2013.

Shalu Arora v.
Tanu Bathla : CRM. No.21798/2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She seeks quashment of the procedure under Section 138 of the Act of 1881.
6. Counsel appearing for the respondents has vehemently opposed the contentions.
It is argued that it is a joint account from which the cheque has been issued but although the same has been signed by the husband of the applicant.
But the fact remains that when it is a joint account then both are liable for the payment towards the instrument.
Therefore, she has been made a party in the proceedings under Section 138 of the Act of 1881.
The learned trial court has rightly taken cognizance of the matter.
He has prayed for dismissal of the application.

7. Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.
The undisputed fact being that the instrumental question has been issued from a joint account of the petitioner as well as her husband Santosh Kumar Agnihotri.
It is not in dispute that the cheque in question has been signed by Santosh Kumar Agnihotri.

From perusal of the complaint in paragraph 2 the respondent has admitted this fact that the cheque bearing No.518676 of Induslnd Bank Ltd. dated 30.11.2017 has been issued from the joint account of the applicant as well as her Dipti Agnihotri vs Smt. Ruchi Agrawal on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130754823/
2 husband.

entities.text: Dipti Agnihotri vs Smt. Ruchi Agrawal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The cheque has been duly signed by Santosh Agnihotri.
Therefore, an application was also filed before the trial court for deleting her name from the proceedings.
But no order has been passed by the learned trial court on the aforesaid application.
On the contrary cognizance has been taken by the learned trial court.

9. The only question which crops up for consideration before this court is whether the petitioner who is not the signatory of the cheque in question is liable for prosecution under Section 138 of the Act of 1881.

10. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Aparna A. Shah v. M/s Sheth Developers P. Ltd. and another : 2013(8)SCC 71 and Alka Khandu Avhad v. Amar Syamprasad Mishra : 2021 (4) SCC 675 has held that it is the drawer of the cheque who can be prosecuted.

entities.text: Aparna A. Shah v. M/s Sheth Developers P. Ltd. and another : 2013(8)SCC 71
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Alka Khandu Avhad v. Amar Syamprasad Mishra : 2021 (4) SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. The plain language of Section 138 of the Act of 1881 refers to payee or the holder in due course of cheque.
It indicates that after the dishonour of the cheque the drawer of the same can be brought to the doc for fault committed by him and not anyone else.

The drawer of the cheque has been defined under Section 7 of the Act of 1881 which signifies that the maker of a bill of exchange or cheque is called the "drawer"; the person thereby directed to pay is called the "drawee".
Admittedly, the instrument in question has been signed by the husband of the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is not liable for making the payments.
12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Aparna A. Shah (supra) has held as under - "21.

The above discussion with reference to Section 138 and the materials culled out from the statutory notice, reply, copy of the complaint, order, issuance of process etc.,
clearly show that only the drawer of the cheque being responsible for the same.
22. In addition to our conclusion, it is useful to refer some of the decisions rendered by various High Courts on this issue.
23. The Learned Single Judge of the Madras High Court in Devendra Pundir vs. Rajendra Prasad Maurya, Proprietor, Satyamev Exports S/o.

entities.text: Devendra Pundir vs. Rajendra Prasad Maurya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Sri Rama Shankar Maurya, 2008 Criminal Law Journal 777, following decisions of this Court, has concluded thus:
"7.
This Court is of the considered view that the above proposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision cited supra is squarely applicable to the facts of the instant case.

Even in this case, as already pointed out, the first accused is admittedly the sole proprietrix of the concern namely, "Kamakshi Enterprises" and as such, the question of the second accused to be vicariously held liable for the offence said to have been committed by the first accused under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act not at all arise."
After saying so, learned Single Judge, quashed the proceedings initiated against the petitioner therein and permitted the Judicial Magistrate to proceed and expedite the trial in respect of others.

Dipti Agnihotri vs Smt. Ruchi Agrawal on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130754823/
3 24.

entities.text: Dipti Agnihotri vs Smt. Ruchi Agrawal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Gita Berry vs. Genesis Educational Foundation, 151 (2008) DLT 155, the petitioner therein was wife and she filed a petition under Section 482 of the Code seeking quashing of the complaint filed under Section 138 of the N.I. Act.

entities.text: Gita Berry vs. Genesis Educational Foundation, 151 (2008) DLT 155
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner therein was that the offence under Section 138 of the Act cannot be said to have been made out against her only on the ground that she was a joint account holder along with her husband.
It was pointed out that she has neither drawn nor issued the cheque in question and, therefore, according to her, the complaint against her was not maintainable.

Learned Single Judge of the High Court of Delhi, after noting that the complaint was only under Section 138 of the Act and not under Section 420 IPC and pointing out that nothing was elicited from the complainant to the effect that the petitioner was responsible for the cheque in question, quashed the proceedings insofar as the petitioner therein.

25. In Smt. Bandeep Kaur vs. S. Avneet Singh, (2008) 2 PLR 796, in a similar situation, learned Single Judge of the Punjab and Haryana High Court held that in case the drawer of a cheque fails to make the payment on receipt of a notice, then the provisions of Section 138 of the Act could be attracted against him only.

entities.text: Smt. Bandeep Kaur vs. S. Avneet Singh, (2008) 2 PLR 796
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Single Judge further held that though the cheque was drawn to a joint bank account which is to be operated by anyone, i.e., the petitioner or by her husband, but the controversial document is the cheque, the liability regarding dishonouring of which can be fastened on the drawer of it.

After saying so, learned Single Judge accepted the plea of the petitioner and quashed the proceedings insofar as it relates to her and permitted the complainant to proceed further insofar as against others.
26. In the light of the principles as discussed in the earlier paras, we fully endorse the view expressed by the learned Judges of the Madras, Delhi and Punjab & Haryana High Courts.
27. In the light of the above discussion, we hold that under Section 138 of the Act, it is only the drawer of the cheque who can be prosecuted.

In the case on hand,
admittedly, the appellant is not a drawer of the cheque and she has not signed the same.
A copy of the cheque was brought to our notice, though it contains name of the appellant and her husband, the fact remains that her husband alone put his signature.

In addition to the same, a bare reading of the complaint as also the affidavit of examination-in- chief of the complainant and a bare look at the cheque would show that the appellant has not signed the cheque.

28. We also hold that under Section 138 of the N.I. Act, in case of issuance of cheque from joint accounts, a joint account holder cannot be prosecuted unless the cheque has been signed by each and every person who is a joint account holder.
The said principle is an exception to Section 141 of the N.I. Act which would have no application in the case on hand.
The proceedings filed under Section 138 cannot be used as an arm twisting tactics to recover the amount allegedly due from the appellant.

It cannot be said that the complainant has no remedy against the appellant Dipti Agnihotri vs Smt. Ruchi Agrawal on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130754823/
4 but certainly not under Section 138.

entities.text: Dipti Agnihotri vs Smt. Ruchi Agrawal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The culpability attached to dishonour of a cheque can, in no case "except in case of Section 141 of the N.I. Act" be extended to those on whose behalf the cheque is issued.
This Court reiterates that it is only the drawer of the cheque who can be made an accused in any proceeding under Section 138 of the Act.

Even the High Court has specifically recorded the stand of the appellant that she was not the signatory of the cheque but rejected the contention that the amount was not due and payable by her solely on the ground that the trial is in progress.
It is to be noted that only after issuance of process, a person can approach the High Court seeking quashing of the same on various grounds available to him.
Accordingly, the High Court was clearly wrong in holding that the prayer of the appellant cannot even be considered.
Further, the High Court itself has directed the Magistrate to carry out the process of admission/denial of documents.
In such circumstances, it cannot be concluded that the trial is in advanced stage."

13. After going through the entire controversy it will be safe to hold that the applicant who is not the signatory of the instrument in question cannot be prosecuted under Section 138 of the Act of 1881,
in view of the settled legal proposition.
14. Under these circumstances, this petition is allowed.
The proceedings 138 of the Act of 1881 as against the petitioner is hereby quashed.
15. The learned trial court is directed to continue the proceedings against the husband of the petitioner who is the signatory holder of the cheque in question.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE LR Dipti Agnihotri vs Smt. Ruchi Agrawal on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130754823/
